findings.title: The aged father turns replacement into a social appeal
findings.claim: By presenting the detained man's father as aged and socially weighty, the brothers turn a request to take one of them in his place into an appeal to care and beneficence: the proposed replacement is framed as a humane answer to a family burden.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers for father, elderhood, age, taking, and one-of-us meet the independent aged-parent, dependent-household, custody, and personal-liability relations supplied by the packet; those contacts make the age description function as the reason for asking the authority to move custody across persons.
findings.reader_payoff: The father's age becomes newly legible as an argument inside the petition, and the offered brother appears as a socially motivated substitute rather than an unexplained exchange.
findings.containment: The plain father, age, and substitution request remain intact. This does not establish that the transfer is legally valid, that the elder is a scholar, or that the brothers' compassion is sincere.

epistemic.reason: The core relation has trusted cross-run support, while the elderhood/status material includes legacy evidence and the connection rows supply target Arabic without target morphology; the result is retained with its boundary visible.

findings.title: Later grief gives the father's age an embodied history
findings.claim: The father's later grief makes the age foregrounded here feel like a lived vulnerability, so the appeal can be heard as more than tactical description while remaining a request for substitution.
findings.mechanism: The focus's elderhood carrier meets the supplied retrospective that cites 12:84-86 as an embodied history of grief; that later context changes how the earlier age description bears on the request.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel why the father's condition carries emotional weight without losing the plain scene in which the brothers are bargaining for a replacement.
findings.containment: This preserves the focus's ordinary age claim and does not infer a settled motive, a completed reconciliation, or legal equivalence between the father and the detained brother.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective is supplied as legacy-unbound reader-walk evidence and names the later ayat, but it does not provide independent target morphology; the reading is retained with attribution and a narrow boundary.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The age description bears the memory of grief while still functioning inside the brothers' substitution request.
branch_activations.boundary: The later history deepens the condition; it does not replace the focus's request with a later scene or settle the brothers' intention.

findings.title: The offered replacement meets a responsibility-bound custody
findings.claim: The request to take one of the brothers in the detained man's place turns a personal custody into a negotiable slot, while the surrounding rule keeps custody tied to the person found with the object; the tension makes the proposed exchange itself part of the ayah's meaning.
findings.mechanism: The focus's taking and place carriers meet 12:75's stated consequence and 12:76's designated custody, while the supplied 12:79 retrospective and wider no-burden and no-ransom connections provide contrary frames; the contacts change a compassionate offer into a visible attempt to move responsibility across persons.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the proposed replacement is ethically and structurally charged: it offers human relief precisely where the surrounding rule has fixed a person to a consequence.
findings.containment: The compassionate plea and the non-transferability frame remain together. This does not decide a legal doctrine, make the later refusal the focus's only meaning, or erase the brothers' family appeal.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective is legacy-unbound, while the same-surah and inter-surah connection rows carry strong prior labels but omit target morphology; the responsibility contrast is therefore explicit but qualified.

branch_activations.boundary: The branch gives a responsibility relation around the taking; it does not pronounce the final legal ruling.

findings.title: Beneficence is recognized before identity is settled
findings.claim: The closing claim that the authority is seen among the benefactors reaches beyond a present compliment: its perception-and-evaluation language repeats an earlier recognition of Joseph, and the later recognition named in the supplied walk lets the praise remain both persuasive and unwittingly true.
findings.mechanism: The focus forms for seeing and doing good return in the exact 12:36 connection and in wider good-doer formulas, while the supplied retrospective says the ruler being praised is later recognized as the brother the speakers harmed; repetition turns social evaluation into dramatic irony without cancelling its rhetorical use.
findings.reader_payoff: The final praise becomes a live act of recognition: the brothers appeal to a beneficent identity before they consciously identify the person who embodies it.
findings.containment: Strategic praise, sincere perception, and later recognition remain co-present. This does not choose the brothers' motive or assert a full surah-wide system from these connections.

epistemic.reason: The repeated phrase and evaluative formulas are supplied in medium-labelled connection rows, while the later recognition comes from a legacy-unbound retrospective without target morphology; the combined reading remains qualified.

findings.title: The plea is addressed to an office of public power
findings.claim: Calling Joseph al-Aziz places the request before a public office whose power and social distance are part of the persuasion, so the family appeal is also a petition to an authority.
findings.mechanism: The focus title carrier meets the same title in 12:30, where the household setting is named around the Aziz; the repeated title connects the official addressee to the earlier household context and makes the brothers' address carry both access to power and remembered relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The vocative becomes more than polite address: it shows why the brothers appeal to this person as the holder of an office capable of deciding custody.
findings.containment: The title remains a human office-title in this focus. The connection does not turn it into a divine name or prove that the brothers consciously recall the earlier household episode.

epistemic.reason: The same-surah connection supplies the exact target Arabic and an explicit title relation, but target morphology is not supplied and the contextual bridge remains an inference.

findings.title: The speech continues a chain of bargaining
findings.claim: The brothers' qālū launches another negotiation: the same group that earlier promised to persuade their father and used recovered goods to secure the brother now presents an alternative to the authority who holds him.
findings.mechanism: The focus speech carrier meets 12:61's explicit undertaking to seek paternal consent and 12:65's persuasive exchange; those wider negotiations make the current direct address a calculated petition with a family-care rationale.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening speech-act becomes part of a continuing strategy of persuasion, so the request's sequence from father-warrant to substitute feels structurally deliberate.
findings.containment: This characterizes the speech act's social form without deciding that every word is deceitful or reducing the request to strategy alone.

epistemic.reason: The same-surah connections explicitly describe the earlier negotiations and supply target Arabic, but target morphology is absent and the characterization of the present speech as negotiation is an inference.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek anlam, iki taraflı konuşup görüşmedir.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 12:61 records their undertaking to persuade the father, and 12:65 records their use of recovered goods and promised measure to persuade him.
branch_activations.activation: The speech carrier meets the earlier bargaining sequence, so the present utterance functions as another two-sided negotiation rather than an isolated report.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The brothers deliberately move from a stated family warrant to an offered alternative within a chain of persuasion.
branch_activations.boundary: The negotiation frame does not prove deception or make the petition purely strategic.

findings.title: The father carries the history of favoritism
findings.claim: The father invoked as vulnerable here is also the paternal relation around which the brothers earlier measured their own exclusion, so the present appeal carries an old family imbalance into the request for substitution.
findings.mechanism: The focus father carrier meets 12:8's explicit complaint about paternal preference; that wider contact changes the appeal from isolated compassion into a petition spoken within a family history of comparison and resentment.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the father's presence has narrative pressure beyond age: the same relationship that gives the appeal emotional force has also been the source of the brothers' grievance.
findings.containment: The family history deepens the present father appeal without making the current request insincere or reducing the father's age to jealousy.

epistemic.reason: The same-surah connection supplies exact target Arabic and directly states the earlier jealousy and paternal favoritism relation; target morphology is absent, so the contextual synthesis remains qualified.

branch_activations.boundary: The contact does not establish a motive for the present speech or turn the age appeal into mere resentment.
